audit_question: Determine which Wild-relevant Hearthstone mechanics and archetype pressures can be lowered directly into HSConfig normal-path runtime config, and which should stay warning-only because the current HSConfig and documented VisionAI surfaces do not expose a safe first-class lowering path.
verdict: The current HSConfig normal path can directly or partially express most Wild mechanic pressure through GlobalValues.json, Mulligan.json, per-card CARDID.json, and Combo.json for exact sequences, but it cannot honestly lower every signature mechanic as a first-class choice surface. In this matrix, 6 mechanic groups are direct enough for normal-path runtime authoring, 13 are only partial and need explicit warning boundaries, and 2 should remain warning-only in the current design: Dredge and Tradeable.

normal_path_surfaces: Combo.json for exact ordered battlecry chains
current_truth.warning_only_boundary: Non-targeted value heuristics still depend on general card-usage lowering rather than a battlecry-only planner.
current_truth.rationale: Battlecry is the cleanest targeted mechanic in the documented card-behavior surface because the current registry and local fixtures already use BeforeBattlecryTargetBonus for exact target posture.

current_truth.warning_only_boundary: Deathrattle trigger ordering, resurrection quality, and generated-body follow-up value remain indirect unless they collapse into simpler play-now or keep-alive posture.
current_truth.rationale: HSConfig can tell the bot when to deploy or preserve a deathrattle minion, but there is no dedicated normal-path deathrattle trigger planner.

current_truth.warning_only_boundary: The respawn value itself is not a first-class runtime block, so only deploy or preserve posture is directly representable.
beyond_current_fixture_examples: Package mechanic across mixed Wild lists rather than a verified dedicated fixture candidate in this audit [uncertain]
current_truth.rationale: Reborn behaves like a persistence modifier on top of minion timing and board value, not like a separate documented choice surface.

current_truth.warning_only_boundary: HSConfig can time the recruiter, but it cannot control which card the deck pulls beyond deck construction and source-backed sequencing context.
beyond_current_fixture_examples: JtU Quest Mage with Guild Recruiter
current_truth.rationale: Current CtAPaladin and BigShaman fixtures already prove recruit timing, but the summon result itself is not a separate runtime choice.

current_truth.warning_only_boundary: Only exact option identities lower cleanly. Unresolved or source-weak discover pools must stay suppressed and warning-visible.
current_truth.rationale: The operator guide and router contract explicitly support discover_choice lowering when the offered option card ids are source-backed.

current_truth.warning_only_boundary: The signature bottom-three choice is not a documented VisionAI choice block, so HSConfig should not pretend Dredge option selection is a direct runtime surface.
current_truth.rationale: Dredge is a real mechanic family in Step 03 taxonomy, but the current documented lowering surfaces do not include a Dredge-choice equivalent to OnDiscoverCardBonus.

current_truth.warning_only_boundary: There is no documented trade-now runtime block, so HSConfig cannot honestly encode the actual trade decision as a first-class behavior.
beyond_current_fixture_examples: Package mechanic across Reno and control lists rather than a verified dedicated archetype in this audit [uncertain]
current_truth.rationale: The local compiler can tag tradeable cards for generic play-timing pressure, but that is not the same as telling the bot when to trade.

current_truth.warning_only_boundary: Exact future-mana planning is still heuristic and deck-level, not a separate documented overload planner.
current_truth.rationale: Overload timing is still a play-now or wait rule, and the current compiler already maps overload roles into BeforePlayCardBonus.

normal_path_surfaces: CARDID.json: BeforeBattlecryTargetBonus when the freeze effect is battlecry-based
CARDID.json: BeforeUseHeroPowerBonus when the freeze effect is hero-power-based
current_truth.warning_only_boundary: Generic targeted freeze spells do not have a dedicated spell-target runtime block, so exact target choice remains warning-boundary work outside battlecry and hero-power cases.
current_truth.rationale: Freeze pressure matters in Wild, but only some freeze delivery paths match the documented target surfaces cleanly.

current_truth.warning_only_boundary: Healing tradeoffs and exact stabilisation thresholds are not exposed as a dedicated normal-path lifesteal surface.
beyond_current_fixture_examples: Mage stabilisation packages with Sleet Skater [uncertain]
current_truth.rationale: HSConfig can prefer using or attacking with a lifesteal source, but it cannot express full heal-threshold planning as a separate mechanic compiler.

normal_path_surfaces: CARDID.json: BeforePhysicalAttackBonus for Rush and Charge
current_truth.warning_only_boundary: Rush and Charge map well to attack posture; Taunt is mostly indirect board-value posture and does not have a dedicated taunt-specific runtime block.
beyond_current_fixture_examples: Aggro and pirate shells with Rush or Charge packages [uncertain]
current_truth.rationale: The grouped mechanic family is not uniform. Rush and Charge are attack-decision mechanics, while Taunt is mostly about defensive board value.

current_truth.warning_only_boundary: Repeated location activations and target use after the card is already in play are not a first-class documented location block in the current HSConfig path.
beyond_current_fixture_examples: Highlander Priest with Cathedral of Atonement
current_truth.rationale: Step 03 treats locations as an explicit card family, but the current normal-path router only gives them generic play-timing treatment.

current_truth.warning_only_boundary: None beyond ordinary exact-sequence limits; this is already a proven mechanic family in current fixtures.
current_truth.rationale: Weapon sequencing and hero-attack posture are among the clearest current HSConfig families, already proven by Kingslayer and Pirate shells.

current_truth.warning_only_boundary: The timing of playing a secret is lowerable, but secret ordering, hidden-information timing traps, and cross-secret layering are not separate documented runtime surfaces.
current_truth.rationale: Secrets are strategically important in Wild, but HSConfig currently treats them as play-timing pressure rather than a first-class secret engine.

normal_path_surfaces: Linked hero-power identity from Step 03 metadata
current_truth.warning_only_boundary: Only unresolved or random hero-power identities should stay warning-only.
beyond_current_fixture_examples: Highlander Priest and XL Shadow Priest with Shadowreaper Anduin and Raza
current_truth.rationale: Hero-power transform is already a named claim kind, an existing fixture family, and a documented card-behavior block.

normal_path_surfaces: Linked entity graph for deterministic hero powers, rewards, and fixed generated cards
CARDID.json for generated cards with resolved identity
current_truth.warning_only_boundary: Random generation pools, untracked option sets, and unstable created-card branches should stay warning-only unless exact identities are source-backed.
beyond_current_fixture_examples: Highlander Priest theft or generation packages
current_truth.rationale: Step 03 explicitly requires generated-entity relationships, but only deterministic or source-resolved identities lower cleanly.

current_truth.warning_only_boundary: Continuous aura math, stacked aura valuation, and full board-state optimisation are broader than the current first-class runtime blocks.
beyond_current_fixture_examples: Board-flood and aura shells rather than one verified extra archetype in this audit [uncertain]
current_truth.rationale: HSConfig can value keeping an aura minion alive or playing it on curve, but not compute every downstream aura interaction directly.

normal_path_surfaces: CARDID.json: BeforePhysicalAttackBonus when discard synergies affect attack posture
current_truth.warning_only_boundary: Exact hidden hand-discard outcomes still follow card rules, but the enabler timing itself is directly lowerable.
beyond_current_fixture_examples: Current Discolock already proves the family; no additional Wild fixture is required right now
current_truth.rationale: The local fixture suite already proves discard as a runtime-lowerable mechanic_usage family.

normal_path_surfaces: CARDID.json: BeforeBattlecryTargetBonus when destroy is battlecry-based
CARDID.json: BeforePhysicalAttackBonus when destroy is attack-based
CARDID.json: BeforePlayCardBonus for untargeted destroy timing
current_truth.warning_only_boundary: Generic targeted destroy spells do not have a dedicated spell-target normal-path block, so exact target choice is only partial today.
current_truth.rationale: Destroy is a delivery-family problem more than a standalone surface: some delivery paths lower, others do not.

normal_path_surfaces: CARDID.json: BeforeBattlecryTargetBonus when silence is battlecry-based
CARDID.json: BeforePlayCardBonus for untargeted or self-silence timing
current_truth.warning_only_boundary: Generic silence-spell target choice is not a documented dedicated surface in the current normal path.
beyond_current_fixture_examples: Highlander Priest with Shard of the Naaru or similar silence packages
current_truth.rationale: Silence behaves like targeted utility. It only becomes fully direct when the delivery path maps to an existing target block.

normal_path_surfaces: CARDID.json: BeforeBattlecryTargetBonus when transform is battlecry-based
CARDID.json: BeforePlayCardBonus for untargeted transform timing
current_truth.warning_only_boundary: Generic spell-based transform target choice and random transform outcomes are not first-class lowerable surfaces.
current_truth.rationale: Transform shares the same delivery-path constraint as silence and destroy: some forms lower cleanly, some remain warning-only.

Read prior HSConfig research artifacts on Step 03 taxonomy, Step 08 card behavior routing, the CardID surface router, and the current runtime-surface contract to keep this matrix aligned with the live local repo instead of the older broader design material.

gaps_or_risks: The current HSConfig compiler is broader than the representative matrix but narrower than the full documented VisionAI block registry. Several mechanics are only partially real in the current implementation even when the registry could theoretically support richer lowering later.

Generic targeted spell mechanics remain the biggest honest boundary. Battlecry targets, hero powers, physical attacks, Discover, and some Choose One flows have direct documented blocks; generic spell targeting does not, so destroy, silence, transform, and some freeze cases remain partial.

Dredge and Tradeable are easy places to over-claim. Timing the card is not the same as lowering the signature Dredge choice or Tradeable action. Those two should stay warning-only until a first-class documented surface exists.

Locations are under-surfaced in the current normal path. The card family is explicit in metadata, but current runtime lowering still treats it mostly as a generic play-timing card instead of a repeated-use object.

Generated entities are a mixed lane. Deterministic linked entities are safe, but random creation pools, unstable token identities, and unresolved discover-like branches can quickly become fabricated behavior if not suppressed visibly.

Some beyond-current archetype examples are package-level rather than dedicated tiered archetypes, so this matrix is stronger on runtime-surface honesty than on claiming a one-deck-per-mechanic Wild taxonomy [uncertain].
deck_set_implications: The current 11-deck HSConfig matrix already covers recruit, deathrattle, discard, combo, hero-power transform, pirate weapon pressure, and board snowball families well enough for source-depth proof. The next useful beyond-current Wild expansion candidates are not more of the same. Secret Mage or a similar secret-heavy Mage row would add Secrets plus real Freeze and Discover pressure in one deck. Overload Shaman would add a clean Overload-first row that the current matrix does not isolate. A Highlander Priest or similar location-heavy control row would add Locations plus practical silence, destroy, and hero-power-swap adjacency. Dredge and Tradeable do not justify a representative fixture until HSConfig grows a direct first-class lowering path for their actual choice or action semantics.
recommended_action: Treat Battlecry, Discover, Overload, Weapons, Hero Power swaps, and Discard as direct enough for normal-path runtime authoring today. Treat Deathrattle, Reborn, Recruit, Freeze, Lifesteal, Taunt/Rush/Charge, Locations, Secrets, generated entities, aura effects, Destroy, Silence, and Transform as partial families that should emit real runtime rows only for the parts that map cleanly to documented blocks, while keeping the rest in warning or suppression reports. Keep Dredge and Tradeable warning-only until there is a documented direct surface for the mechanic itself instead of only a timing proxy. If the matrix is widened, prioritise one Secret Mage style deck, one Overload Shaman style deck, and one location-heavy Priest or control deck before inventing narrower fixture rows.
confidence: High for the runtime-surface classifications and current local HSConfig boundaries; medium for some beyond-current archetype examples where the mechanic is more of a package than a stable dedicated Wild archetype. The support verdicts are grounded mainly in the live HSConfig code, active operator docs, and fixture tests, with current Wild deck pages used as contemporary stress examples rather than as the primary runtime-contract authority.
